newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech fund RIF to make shares tradable.
newsitem.headline: Czech fund RIF to make shares tradable.

text.p: Shareholders of the Czech investment fund Restitucni a Investicni Fond a.s. (RIF) voted on Friday to convert its non-tradable shares into publicly-tradable stock, chairman Jan Kalfus said.

Kalfus, newly elected at Friday's general meeting, said that current shareholders would be able to convert the old shares for new ones with a 1,000 crown nominal value with voting rights on a one-for-one basis.
The conversion should be finalised by next April, Kalfus told a news conference.
The state-run privatisation agency, the National Property Fund (NPF) now holds a 36 percent stake in the RIF and a "golden share" with a veto power over key decisions.
The RIF fund was established by the Czech government and was given a three percent stake of every company privatised during the country's economic reform process.
Some of its shares were granted as compensation for property confiscated ealrier by the communists during their 40-year rule.
Kalfus said that RIF wanted to be listed on the London Stock Exchange within two to three years.
He said the fund had chosen Coopers and Lybrand to audit its books.
